title: UOBYQA: unconstrained optimization by quadratic approximation
contribution: Describes the UOBYQA Fortran code: a trust-region method on full quadratic interpolation models that keeps all Lagrange functions explicitly and uses them for model updates, geometry (model) steps, and an error-bound-based test that saves evaluations; numerics cover accuracy, rounding, kinks and cost, with an explicit n <= 20 (O(n^4)) limit (read from DAMTP 2000/NA14).
problem_entry: Software-first entry: a DFO code for smooth unconstrained problems that tolerates noise better than finite differences, with the O(n^4) scaling limit stated in the abstract (p. 1-2).
key_idea: Keep and update every Lagrange function of the (n+1)(n+2)/2-point interpolation problem, and use them for the model update, the geometry step max|l_j|, and the error bound |Q-F| <= (M/6) sum |l_i| ||x-x_i||^3 with M/6 estimated online (p. 3, p. 10, p. 16-17).
assumptions: No derivatives or constraints; the error bound assumes bounded third derivatives, a view the paper concedes is academic; superlinear convergence is only conjectured, under bounded third derivatives, convergence to a positive-definite minimum and bounded Lagrange functions; finite termination rests on finite precision (p. 10, p. 25).
proof_devices: self-correcting Lagrange update (4.10)-(4.11): the conditions at the moved point are restored exactly whatever the old errors (p. 16-17)
determinant factor: replacing x_t multiplies the interpolation determinant by l_t(new point) (p. 18)

crude max|l_j| on a ball with factor-1/2 guarantee (2.11), top-eigenvector surrogate from span{w, G w} with 0.5 n^{-1/2} spectral-radius bound (2.15), counterexample matrix (2.13), angle grid loss (12+2*sqrt2)/17 ~ 0.872 (p. 7-9)
More-Sorensen trust-region solve after orthogonal tridiagonalization; stop when ratio (2.5) <= 0.01 (p. 5-6)
online estimate of M/6 as the running max of observed |Q-F| / sum|l_i| ||x-x_i||^3 (3.2) (p. 10)
scalar-product trick Q(x_k+d)-Q(x_k)=v_Q^T w, built in O(n^2) (5.4)-(5.7) (p. 20-21)
cheap Frobenius-norm sufficient test (5.9) to skip subproblem solves (p. 22)
heuristic superlinear-convergence argument (p. 24-25) and finite-termination counting argument using finite machine precision (p. 25)
experiments: Random trigonometric sums of squares (Fletcher-Powell 1963), n = 3, 5, 10, 20, 5 instances each, rho 0.1 -> 1e-8, NFTOT per instance, per-rho traces, a +1e4 rounding test, kinked variants (one fails), cost fit 0.8n^2+8.2n+2, per-task timings, Rosenbrock, the singular function, and Chebyquad vs Powell 1964 counts from Fletcher 1965 (p. 22-30).
positioning: A development of COBYLA (1994) and the 1998 survey; Winfield 1973 credited with the idea; Conn-Scheinberg-Toint 1997 distinguished because they do not use Lagrange functions; the only baseline is his own 1964 method; 12 references, 5 by Powell (p. 4, p. 23, p. 31).
writing: Organised as a software description with an 11-step summary; design choices justified by development numerics; limits in the abstract; conjecture hedged and the gap admitted (p. 1, p. 18-20, p. 24-25).
limits_future: O(n^4) work, prohibitive beyond about 50 variables; quadratics model kinks poorly; rounding sets a floor on useful rho; future: a sparse-Hessian version and methods that do not need all Lagrange parameters (the seed of NEWUOA) (p. 26-30).

It would be better, however, to establish this property without some of the assumptions that have been made.

title: On trust region methods for unconstrained minimization without derivatives
contribution: Sets out one interpolation trust-region framework for any linear model space, compares linear (COBYLA), full-quadratic (UOBYQA), sparse (UOBSQA) and diagonal (UOBDQA) models on sparse and random trigonometric problems, and first reports least-Frobenius-norm updating with 2n+1 conditions, which solves n = 160 in fewer evaluations than a quadratic has parameters (read from DAMTP 2002/NA02).
problem_entry: A cost trade-off over model spaces of dimension m: full quadratics give O(n^4) work (intolerable beyond about 50 variables), linear models lack curvature; is a diagonal-Hessian space (m = 2n+1) enough? Expectations are stated before the tests (p. 2-3).
key_idea: A generic framework (trust-region vs model iterations, F only if the step >= rho/2, ratio 0.1, move the centre on any decrease, Lagrange-function updates) with only the model space swapped; then least-Frobenius-norm change of the Hessian, by analogy with symmetric Broyden, to get full quadratics from 2n+1 conditions (p. 4-9, p. 17-19).
assumptions: No derivatives; no convergence theorem; UOBYQA's error estimate is used for UOBDQA although it is invalid there, in order to test empirically; the section-5 rank conditions on X and B; the projection property only for quadratic F; the prototype is not rotation-invariant (p. 11, p. 18-20).
proof_devices: induction on the first singularity: the new system is singular iff l_t(new point) = 0 (p. 7)
O(m^2) update of all Lagrange functions argued optimal-order because the matrix has m^2 entries (p. 8-9)
two-variable quadratic counterexamples with one huge parameter for the linear (3.1)-(3.2) and diagonal (3.3)-(3.6) model classes (p. 9-12)
ill-conditioning explained through Hessian = 2 Z^T Z at the solution and its least eigenvalue (4.5)-(4.6) (p. 14-15)
projection/Pythagoras property of the least-Frobenius update for quadratic F via one-parameter minimization (5.6)-(5.8) (p. 18-19)
KKT form Hessian_new = Hessian_old + sum lambda_j x_j x_j^T with X lambda = 0, giving the saddle system (5.11) with A_ij = (x_i^T x_j)^2/2 (p. 19)
experiments: ARWHEAD, BDQRTIC, CHROSEN at n = 10-25 (rho 0.5 -> 1e-6); random trigonometric family with n or 2n terms, 5 fixed-seed instances, min-max reported; a scaled variant designed after a surprise; timings to n = 40; section-5 prototype to n = 160 (two instances, about 25 h each); metric: number of F values (p. 12-21).
positioning: Contrast with simulated annealing and line searches; Winfield 1973 lacked robust nonsingularity; CST 1997 noted; symmetric Broyden (Fletcher 1987) as the template; baselines are only his own codes; 10 references, 4 by Powell (p. 2, p. 10, p. 17, p. 22).
writing: Main results in the abstract; expectations before results; surprises labelled in the first person ('staggering and unexplained'); an explicit note that the work is incomplete ('jumping the gun'); one arithmetic slip (13122 for 13041 parameters) (p. 1, p. 3, p. 13, p. 19-21).
limits_future: UOBDQA is inefficient on ill-conditioned or non-diagonal Hessians; the prototype is not rotation-invariant; the direct O((m+n)^3) solve is to be replaced by an updating technique; the model's parameters need not all be accurate, which points to new algorithms (p. 12, p. 15-16, p. 19-21).

title: An Interview with M. J. D. Powell (Bulletin of the International Center for Mathematics, n. 14, June 2003)
contribution: A first-person account of Powell's research process: numerical experience as the main source of ideas, conjectures settled by proof or counterexample, exact-arithmetic-first design with stability properties, subroutine-reliability code discipline, zero tolerance for test failures, working alone on uncrowded topics, and strict refereeing and PhD standards (interview, not a research paper).
problem_entry: Problems chosen where a new algorithm he has in mind would help, not from reading others' papers; students steered to topics with little attention (p. 3, p. 5).
key_idea: Research loop: numerical testing suggests convergence and accuracy properties, the conjectures are settled by proofs or counterexamples, and both good and bad features of numerical results are exploited (p. 2-3).
assumptions: New methods are invented assuming exact arithmetic; stability properties let the matrix details be settled after the principal features are chosen (p. 4).
proof_devices: examples and counterexamples as the partner of proofs (p. 2)
hand calculations still used occasionally (p. 2)
experiments: Stance, not experiments: numerical results are the main source of ideas; a 10% failure rate on test problems is intolerable; SA/GA are extravagant in function evaluations (p. 3-4).
positioning: Does not study others' software or papers in detail; considers refereed submissions in isolation (self-admitted gap); credits Davidon for DFP; mostly single-authored by choice (p. 3-6).
writing: Documentation should state what programs can do, with few internal comments; subroutine reliability over formal structure; refereeing checks substantial contribution, correctness and the right amount of detail, line by line (p. 4-5).
limits_future: Open: RBF convergence orders at edges, seen numerically but not proved; the nonlinear optimization book postponed; TOLMIN limited to a few hundred variables; most gratifying paper: the augmented Lagrangian source (p. 6-7).

title: Least Frobenius norm updating of quadratic models that satisfy interpolation conditions
contribution: Formulates the least-Frobenius-norm model update as an (m+n+1)x(m+n+1) saddle system whose inverse H holds the Lagrange-function coefficients, and gives a stable O((m+n)^2) rank-two update of H, an x0-shift procedure, and a constant-term-free variant; stress tests show errors do not grow and are self-corrected (read from DAMTP 2002/NA08).
problem_entry: The predecessor's measured limit (UOBYQA prohibitive at about n = 50; 20 -> 1087 s from n = 20 to 40) plus the S047 prototype (n = 160 in 9688 evaluations vs 13041 parameters) lead to the question of how to update in O(m^2) without serious loss of accuracy when m = O(n) (p. 3-6).
key_idea: Minimize ||Hessian(Q+) - Hessian(Q)||_F subject to m interpolation conditions (chosen for shift-of-origin invariance and uniqueness, by analogy with symmetric Broyden); keep H = W^{-1} and update it by a rank-two formula; store the Hessian implicitly; shift x0; suppress constant terms (p. 4-5, p. 8, p. 13-24).
assumptions: (A1) independent interpolation constraints; (A2) no nonzero linear polynomial vanishes on the points; m >= n+2; one point replaced per update; no fitting; the projection property only for quadratic F; the stability analysis ignores current-iteration rounding (p. 2, p. 4, p. 7, p. 14).
proof_devices: KKT conditions -> saddle system W (2.8); symmetry of G comes out automatically (p. 7-8)
A positive semidefinite by a sum-of-squares rewrite (2.10) (p. 8-9)
projection/Pythagoras property (1.8) via one-parameter Frobenius minimization (p. 9-10)
Lagrange functions = columns of H = W^{-1} (3.3)-(3.4) (p. 10)
inheritance of (A1)/(A2) whenever l_t(x+) != 0 (p. 11)
rank-two inverse update (4.2)/(4.12), proved by checking H+ times each column of W+ (p. 14-17)
error-propagation invariant: Xi = W - H^{-1}; the update zeros the t-th row and column and leaves the rest unchanged (4.1) (p. 14)
Lemma 1: the leading m x m block of H is independent of x0 (p. 18-19)
Lemma 2: alpha, beta >= 0 via the sign structure of the saddle-matrix block inverse, plus a tiny-perturbation device for alpha = 0 (p. 21-22)
cancellation analysis: errors of order M^4 times machine precision when ||x0 - x_b|| = M*Delta (p. 19)
Lemma 3: the self-correcting set of valid Lagrange conditions grows monotonically for the Omega update (p. 26-28)
magnitude bookkeeping of the W and H blocks in powers of Delta (7.12)-(7.13) (p. 34)
experiments: Stress tests of the update only: n = 50, m = 101, random points in a ball, up to 1e5 iterations; tests on the choice of t (max |l| vs oldest eligible point), a far x0, injected 1e-4 errors, and shrinking Delta with x0 = 0 or 1e4*e; log10 error measures of the HW - I blocks; failures (Test 4, Test 7) published (p. 29-35).
positioning: The DFO analogue of symmetric Broyden (Fletcher 1987) and of Broyden-Dennis-More 1973; directly challenges the common advice to update factorizations rather than inverses; 8 references, 4 by Powell (p. 4-5, p. 35-36).
writing: Two numbered reasons plus a roadmap; long algebra suppressed with an admission; a skippable lemma flagged; numerical origin of Lemma 3 disclosed; 'triumph' reserved for Test 5; dedicated to Fletcher (p. 1, p. 5-6, p. 14, p. 26, p. 30, p. 32).
limits_future: The x0 shift costs O(n^3); m, the point-removal rule and the trust-region solver are left open; the (7.5) precaution breaks exact error cancellation; Test 7 fails without x0 shifts; Fortran software (NEWUOA) begun, a CG trust-region solver expected (p. 6, p. 13, p. 19, p. 31, p. 33, p. 35).

method_links.note: formal source: variational problem, (m+n+1) system, Lagrange functions from H, O((m+n)^2) update; the Frobenius norm is justified by shift invariance, uniqueness and the monotone projection property, answering part of the 'norm is debatable' limitation

stability invariant, M^4 cancellation analysis and x0 shift, constant-term suppression, implicit Hessian to meet the O(m^2) budget, code precaution (7.5), inverses over factorizations
